headline: Wall Street Wakes to a Split Market: Geopolitical Crosscurrents Set the Tone for Thursday's Open
body_html:
Futures point to a cautious open on Thursday as traders digest a complex overnight backdrop. Asian equities slipped on a broad pullback in technology shares, while the yen and dollar drifted amid lingering uncertainty over Iran nuclear talks and ahead of closely watched payroll data. Gold climbed to a seven-week high as investors weighed the prospect of the Strait of Hormuz reopening, a development that would carry significant consequences for energy markets globally.

Wednesday's session offered a tale of two markets. The Dow closed at a record, buoyed by Middle East optimism, while the Nasdaq lagged as semiconductor and solar names absorbed heavy selling. Breadth in our universe reflected the tension: 305 names declined against 242 advancers out of 549 tracked. Materials led all sectors, up 2.09%, and Homebuilders added 1.54%, but Semiconductors shed 2.93% and Energy fell 2.62% as Iran-deal progress injected caution into crude positioning.

At the open, watch the energy complex closely — oil edged higher overnight on investor skepticism over the pace of Iran-Oman negotiations, even as diplomatic channels remain active. The Iran headline risk cuts in both directions: a breakthrough compresses oil, a breakdown lifts it. Earnings-driven single-stock volatility from Wednesday's session will also carry momentum into early trading.

briefs.headline: Iran Talks Keep Currency and Commodity Markets on Edge
briefs.body: The dollar and yen drifted through the overnight session as traders remained uncertain about the trajectory of Iran diplomacy. Gold's advance to a seven-week peak suggests haven demand is building, even as oil held relatively steady on cautious optimism that Hormuz-related supply disruptions may eventually ease.

briefs.headline: Middle East Tensions Flare on Two Fronts Simultaneously
briefs.body: Israeli forces struck targets in southern Lebanon following the killing of soldiers, while diplomatic efforts continued in Rome. The dual-track dynamic — military escalation in one theater, negotiations in another — underscores the fragile geopolitical environment that has been a persistent driver of commodity and safe-haven pricing this week.

briefs.headline: Shopify Surges Nearly 17% on Earnings Momentum
briefs.body: Shopify was the standout performer among major technology names on Wednesday, vaulting 16.98% to rank as the second-largest gainer in our universe. The e-commerce platform's sharp advance suggests its latest results significantly exceeded market expectations, offering a bright spot in an otherwise bruised technology landscape.

briefs.headline: Materion Rockets 31% After Advanced-Materials Catalyst
briefs.body: Specialty materials producer Materion posted the session's largest single-stock gain, surging 30.81% in heavy volume. The move elevated the broader Materials sector to the top of Wednesday's sector leaderboard, with a 2.09% advance, as investors responded enthusiastically to what appears to have been a significant company-specific development.

briefs.headline: SolarEdge and Teradata Lead a Brutal Day for Losers
briefs.body: SolarEdge collapsed 30.48% and Teradata fell 23.73%, headlining a painful session for the bottom of the tape. Healthcare devices also drew sellers, with LeMaitre Vascular off 25.32% and Insulet sliding 20.12%, suggesting earnings disappointments cascaded through multiple pockets of the market simultaneously.

briefs.headline: Etsy Cuts 12% of Staff in Structural Overhaul
briefs.body: Online marketplace Etsy announced it would eliminate roughly 12% of its workforce as part of a broader restructuring effort. The move signals continued pressure on mid-tier e-commerce platforms to rationalize costs, even as rival eBay offered an upbeat revenue outlook driven by momentum in higher-value merchandise categories.
